claim: Table C.1 row: the Talos report is the threat report the Muddy Water flow cites, and (with G0069) supports its c1 class (stole data, did not impede systems).
quote:
Campaigns carried
out by the threat actor aim to achieve either of three outcomes:
Espionage  - Supporting the political dominance of the nation state in the Middle East.
locator: PDF p. 2 (web page, unpaginated), 'MuddyWater threat actor'
issue: The report describes the campaign the flow draws (Turkey, malicious PDFs/XLS, PowerShell downloaders), but it reports no data theft in that campaign: its downloader collects only 'preliminary data' (PDF p. 7), and theft appears only as one of the group's three general aims, beside ransomware 'to ... disrupt operations'. 'Stole data' rests on the CTID analyst's 'Exfiltrate intellectual property' node and G0069, not on this report; the report supports at most an espionage motive.

claim: Muddy Water's threat report describes no encryption (for impact) in this campaign.
quote:
Ransomware attacks - MuddyWater has previously attempted to deploy ransomware such as Thanos on
victim networks to either destroy evidence of their intrusions or disrupt operations of private organizations.
locator: PDF p. 2 (web page, unpaginated), 'MuddyWater threat actor'
issue: Absence claim, checked over the whole saved text: ransomware is named only as the group's past attempts ('previously'), and the only encryption in the campaign is the C2 output being 'AES encrypted and returned to the C2' (PDF p. 7), which is communication, not impact. Adversarial read: 'no encryption' could be read to cover the C2 AES; the sentence's context (Data Encrypted for Impact) makes the impact sense plain. Holds.
